messages:
alice_support: FYI Acme reporting repeated 502/504s hitting hosted inferencing. They say SDK retries spiraled and billing jumped overnight. attaching their repro steps and sample request/resp IDs. can someone triage?

ben_eng: Thx. can you paste the request-id and approximate times? also what's the payload size?

alice_support: request-id: req_2026-04-15_11:03:21_acme_42, saw errors around 2026-04-15T11:03:20Z -> 11:08:05Z. payload ~6.4MB (long system prompt + few docs). sdk: acme-js v1.4.2 with default keepalive. example client call they sent:
```
await client.responses.create({model: 'redwood-large-1', input: bigPrompt, stream: true})
```

dave_support: they reported SDK retried 4x quickly, then backoff. billing shows token spike matching retries. temporary mitigation requested by customer: throttle + fallback to smaller model.

carla_sre: two quick hypotheses: 1) edge gateway connection eviction/keepalive mismatch for large streaming requests -> mid-stream 502s; 2) auth refresh storm causing backend fanout when many clients hit token refresh simultaneously. checking edge proxy logs and auth service traces now.

alerts-bot: incident created: INC-3234567 - hosted-inference 5xx spike (support escalated) — priority: high

ben_eng: can you grep the edge logs for that req id and the source IP? also check upstream (inference runtime) error logs for KV cache OOM or OOM during chunked decode.

carla_sre: found the conn at edge: 11:03:21 accepted, large body streamed, then `RST_STREAM` from edge at 11:03:23, upstream returned `502` with grpc error: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` on model-host-12. lots of simultaneous requests from the same tenant between 11:02-11:06 (burst ~120 reqs/min).

alice_support: customer says their client lib attempted to keep 20 concurrent streams without jitter during a migration, so that explains the fanout. they didn't expect to hammer hosted endpoint.

ben_eng: ok that matches. runtime logs show `batch_queue_full` and `kvcache_lock_timeout` warnings right before the 502s. runtime then returned 502 for a few percent of requests; edge converted some to 504s for long waits.

carla_sre: immediate mitigations:
- applied tenant rate-limit at edge for tenant-acme to 30 concurrent streams
- enabled quick-drop fallback to smaller quantized model for excess requests
- added temporary backpressure config on model-host-12

alice_support: notified Acme of temporary rate-limits and fallback. asked them to throttle client concurrency and add exponential jitter.

dave_support: customer accepted fallback for now. asked for recommended SDK changes. proposed guidance: reduce default concurrency, set `maxSockets` and `keepAlive` to sane numbers, add jittered exponential backoff. sample snippet sent: 
```js
const agent = new https.Agent({keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 8});
// add jittered backoff on retries (base 200ms, jitter up to 100ms)
```

ben_eng: follow-ups for eng: add server-side detection for token-refresh storms -> rate-limit auth refresh endpoint per tenant; tune batching to defend against sudden high-concurrency long-prompt streams. also add clearer 429 with Retry-After when we hit tenant-side concurrency caps so SDKs can react.

carla_sre: created two tasks: SRE-4321 (adjust batching thresholds & backpressure) and SRE-4322 (auth refresh rate-limiter per-tenant). assigning owners.

alice_support: quick note for billing: marked spike as mitigated and flagged for review — will contact finance for potential credit as this was caused by client misconfiguration + lack of clearer Retry-After signals.

ben_eng: can engineering reproduce locally? try sending multiple 6MB streaming requests in parallel to a staging model host to see where queue/backpressure surfaces. I'll spin up a repro harness.

carla_sre: status update: edge rate-limit and fallback reduced error rate from ~6% -> ~0.2% for this tenant. keeping mitigations for 24h. will follow up with RCA after analysis.

alice_support: thanks all, I've updated the Acme thread and will close this support ticket once RCA is published.

dave_support: customer wants a short runbook for devs — I'll draft and add to docs: recommended client concurrency defaults, keepalive settings, and how to detect retry storms.

carla_sre: leaving a note: long prompts that keep model runtime busy are high-risk for queue amplification. longer-term: add per-tenant queuing fairness and early 429 path.

ben_eng: +1. assign to backlog after postmortem.

alice_support: closing loop for now, will update when RCA done. :white_check_mark:
